items.prompt: White is well ahead in material. A rule of thumb says that trading pieces helps the side that is ahead. Is there a good trade here? Find the best move.

claims.statement: The engine rates the position at least 400 centipawns in White's favour (depth 16).
Rxe6 is the engine's best move.
An enemy rook stands on e6, so Rxe6 is a capture and the opponent can take back.
Rxe6 is a trade: material changes by at most one point once the exchanges settle (the check allows plus or minus 1).
Ref1 is at least 100 centipawns worse than Rxe6.

hints: You are ahead. List the pieces you would be glad to swap off and the enemy pieces that are still active.
Black's rook on e6 is the most active black piece, and a White rook on the e-file attacks it.
Take the rook on e6 with your rook; Black has to take back.
items.explain: The engine rates the position at least 400 centipawns in White's favour and puts Rxe6 first, at least 100 centipawns above Ref1 (depth 16). Black recaptures, so a pair of rooks goes off and White's extra material stays on the board. Black's most active piece is gone. That trading when ahead is a good plan is a rule of thumb [I]; here it is only one position at one search depth.
